column18: THE ONLY MEASURED PHOTON DOSE GRADIENT IN THE ENTIRE AUDIT, AND hamiltonian_radiation STILL CANNOT BE IDENTIFIED FROM IT. The biological observable is colony DIAMETER — an areal growth measurement — and an areal experiment cannot identify a directional term no matter how well the field is characterised: there is no measured redistribution of biomass along the gradient, only a scalar per colony. The gradient itself is MicroShield point-kernel modelling spot-validated by two TLD readings, one of which disagreed with the model by a factor of two (about 100 rad measured against about 50 rad predicted), and the total dose is 0.5-1 Gy over seven days, three to four orders of magnitude below every other ionizing record here. On melanin: pigmentation INCREASED under UV and DECREASED under gamma, both at P < 0.001 in both species, and growth rate did not change under gamma at all (P = 0.255 and P = 0.615) — so any pigmentation-versus-dose result imported from a UV study carries the WRONG SIGN applied to gamma. The measurement is a mean grey value, an optical proxy on an image, not a pigment mass; the biological replicate count is not stated, and a P-value without an n cannot be propagated; the species is not C. sphaerospermum and the isolates carry no culture-collection accession, so they are neither obtainable nor re-identifiable.

column18: THREE REFUSALS RECORDED AS EVIDENCE, because a refusal that is not written down gets re-derived. The 1.09 g/cm3 is a CELL BUOYANT density from density-gradient centrifugation: it excludes the matrix and the pore water and overstates the bulk by roughly the void fraction, while density_basis must be wet_bulk — dimensionally plausible, widely cited, easy to justify in a sentence, and wrong. The biofilm concentrations are cited to Nielsen 1997 and Laspidou & Rittmann 2002, so they are declared rather than measured on that system, and they were read inside a 2 x 2 x 2 mm3 NMR voxel three orders of magnitude coarser than any plausible pitch. A biomass objective function is a declared stoichiometry frequently borrowed wholesale from E. coli, on a dry basis, failing both the evidence rule and the basis rule.
